data.name: Badrah
data.gender_notes: Badrah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In the night, the moon shines brightly and lights up the dark sky, just like the name Badrah. This name is derived from the Arabic word ‘badr’, meaning 'moon' or 'full moon'. It is a beautiful name for a baby girl, full of spiritual significance and meaning. The name Badrah carries the meaning “Moonlight” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Badrah usually hope their child will grow to embody moonlight and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine guidance and protection.
data.etymology: Badrah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moonlight.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Badrah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_english.name: Badrah
in_english.meaning: Badrah means full moon and radiant light in Arabic
in_english.long_meaning: Badrah is a female given name derived from Arabic roots, specifically from the word 'badr' which means full moon. In Islamic tradition, the name Badrah symbolizes completion, illumination, and spiritual guidance. The name is mentioned in the Quran and holds significant cultural and spiritual importance across Muslim communities worldwide

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic tradition, language and culture are deeply interconnected. Names hold great significance in the Muslim community, often derived from religious or symbolic meanings. The name Badrah reminds us of the historical battle of Badr, which is among the most important events in Islamic history. This battle was a turning point in the early history of the Islamic Ummah (community) and took place in 624 AD, just two years after the migration of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from Mecca to Medina. The Battle of Badr marked the first significant military victory for the nascent Muslim community. Conquering the fearsome Meccan army, the Muslims not only gained a military victory but also secured their survival in the face of grave odds.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Badrah holds considerable spiritual significance as it reflects the role of the moon in Islamic belief. The moon is considered sacred and is mentioned frequently in the Quran. It is believed that God created the night and the day, the sun, and the moon. Allah says in Surah Ar-Ra'd (Quran 13:2), "It is Allah who erected the heavens without any pillars that you [can] see; is firm and steadfast; the sun and the moon [are designated] for a term. That is the correction and the explanation of all things and the ordinance. And Allah, your God, has decreed that the people should not [be left] except under a leader. Whenever they believe in Allah and in what has been sent down to you, and they have surrendered [to Allah]
